release.notes:
First release published to npm through trusted publishing (OIDC). npm had 1.36.4; 1.36.5 and 1.37.0 were tagged before the npm-publish job existed.

### Documentation

- `docs/PHANTOM-USAGE.md`: using the plugin under `phantom exec` (placeholders, session detection, `phm:` references not resolved), the base URL and key settings that exist, and LiteLLM 1.83.0 or newer (prefer a current release).

### Security

- The Anthropic summarizer no longer falls back to the Claude Code OAuth token (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`) when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points anywhere other than `https://api.anthropic.com`. With a LiteLLM or other proxy configured and no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, that token was sent to the proxy as `x-api-key`. Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (or a `phm_` placeholder) to use a proxy.
- `ashlr__orient` no longer reads an `endpointOverride` tool argument. A model could pass it to choose where the local-LLM key and project excerpts were sent. The endpoint now comes only from `ASHLR_LLM_URL`.
- `ashlr__genome_consolidate` no longer uses its `model` argument as an endpoint URL. A model could pass a URL there to choose where the local-LLM key and genome content were sent. `model` now only selects `none` (offline) or LLM merging; the endpoint comes only from `ASHLR_LLM_URL`.
- The "local LLM unreachable" stderr warning names the endpoint as `scheme://host:port` only. It printed the full `ASHLR_LLM_URL`, including any credentials, path or query.
- `scripts/genome-key.ts import <genomeId>` reads the team key from stdin (hidden at a terminal, or piped), so it no longer has to be passed as an argument, where other local users could see it in `ps` and it stayed in shell history. A key given as a third argument still works but prints a warning. An invalid key is rejected without echoing any of it.
- `server/src/cli/cap-check.ts` reads the user API token from stdin (hidden at a terminal, or piped) instead of requiring it as an argument, where other local users could see it in `ps` and it stayed in shell history. A token given as an argument still works but prints a warning. The token is never printed.
- The Anthropic and cloud summarizers redact key material from an endpoint's error body before putting it in the thrown error. A gateway that quoted the rejected `x-api-key` or pro token back in a 401 put it into the error message. Any run of 8 or more characters found in a configured key (`ASHLR_LLM_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ASHLR_EMBED_KEY`, `ASHLR_PRO_TOKEN`, `PHANTOM_PROXY_TOKEN`, or the `~/.ashlr/pro-token` file) is replaced with `[redacted]`. A new test drives every keyed caller through each gateway refusal and network-error path and fails if any key appears in an error, a return value, stdout or stderr.
- `scripts/deploy-smoke.sh` sends the `ASHLR_TOKEN` bearer header to curl through a config on stdin instead of a `-H` argument, so the token is no longer visible to other local users in `ps`.

### Changed

- `ashlr-plugin codex-doctor` (text output) adds an `MCP launch` line saying whether `ashlr-mcp`, the command in the plugin's `.mcp.json`, is on PATH. When it is not, the line gives the fix: install the package bin, or point the host at the printed source-checkout command. Report-only: the `ok` verdict and the `--json` report are unchanged.
- `ashlr__orient`'s LLM call follows the gateway rules on the default path: `ASHLR_LLM_URL` must be https, or http only to `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`; credentials in the URL are refused; redirects are not followed. The default is now `http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1` (was `http://localhost:1234/v1`). Breaks a documented use: `ASHLR_LLM_URL=http://localhost:...` is refused for orient (it falls back to its plain file summary); use `http://127.0.0.1:...` instead.
- `ashlr__genome_consolidate`'s LLM merge follows the same rules on the default path, with the same `http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1` default. Breaks two documented uses: passing a base URL as `model` (for example `http://localhost:1234/v1`) no longer selects the endpoint, so set `ASHLR_LLM_URL` instead; and `ASHLR_LLM_URL=http://localhost:...` is refused, so genome merging falls back to sequential-apply. Use `http://127.0.0.1:...`.
- The keyed Anthropic and OpenAI calls (summarizer, token measurement, genome auto-consolidate reachability probes) follow the same default-path rules for `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and `OPENAI_BASE_URL`: https, or http only to `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`; credentials in the URL are refused; redirects are not followed, so `x-api-key` never follows one. The defaults and the Phantom proxy (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...`) are unaffected. Breaks a documented use: a gateway on plain http to any other host, including `http://localhost:...`, is refused (the call fails like a network error and falls back); use `http://127.0.0.1:...` or https.
- The pro-token cloud route (`ASHLR_API_URL`), the local provider (`ASHLR_LLM_URL`, probe and chat) and the internal legacy summarizer endpoint follow the same default-path rules, so the pro token and `ASHLR_LLM_KEY` go only to https or to `127.0.0.1` / `[::1]` and never follow a redirect. The local default is now `http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1` (was `http://localhost:1234/v1`); the hosted default `https://api.ashlr.ai` is unchanged. Breaks a documented use: `ASHLR_LLM_URL` or `ASHLR_API_URL` set to plain http on any other host, including `http://localhost:...`, is refused and summarization falls back to truncation; use `http://127.0.0.1:...` or https.

### Added

- Opt-in OpenAI-compatible embeddings (`ASHLR_EMBED_FORMAT=openai`, off by default), for a LiteLLM proxy or any `/v1/embeddings` server. The plugin POSTs `{ model, input }` to `<ASHLR_EMBED_URL>/embeddings` with an optional `ASHLR_EMBED_KEY`, under the gateway rules: https, or http only to `127.0.0.1` / `[::1]`; no credentials in the URL; no redirects. Strict mode adds the allowlist. A Phantom `phm_` placeholder is sent unchanged for the proxy to swap. A `phm:` reference is never resolved. The key and the embedded text are never logged. Without the variable the Ollama format is unchanged. See docs/embeddings-gateway.md.
- Opt-in strict gateway targets for keyed model calls (`ASHLR_GATEWAY_STRICT=1`, off by default). A key goes only to `127.0.0.1` / `[::1]`, an exact https `host:port` in `ASHLR_GATEWAY_HOSTS`, or the built-in provider hosts on 443; credentials in the URL and redirects are refused, and refusals name the host only. Covers the local, legacy, Anthropic and cloud providers, token measurement, `ashlr__orient` and `ashlr__genome_consolidate` endpoints, and the genome auto-consolidate probes. With the variable unset nothing changes. See docs/llm-providers.md.
- `scripts/bench-read-real.ts` prints report-only recommended thresholds for the read redirect (current 2048 B) and the TS/JS AST skeleton (current 6144 B), derived by break-even over 256 B size bins with at least 3 files each, plus how they were derived and the caveat that they come from this repo's own files with estimated tokens. No default changes. `--no-thresholds` skips the extra AST reads.
- `ashlr doctor` and `run-benchmark --validate-tokenizer` recognise a `phantom exec -- <cmd>` session from variable names, `phm` prefixes and the proxy host and port: the doctor adds a `phantom exec` line (proxy port, placeholder key names, proxied base URLs with the session token redacted) and warns for a placeholder outside a session, a placeholder whose base URL bypasses the proxy, or a `phm:` reference. Nothing is resolved or revealed and no value is printed. The benchmark skips its API sample when the key would not work.
- `ashlr doctor` shows whether the optional Phantom CLI is installed and its version, in the install section. It only runs `phantom --version`. It never runs `phantom reveal`, never reads the vault or `.env` files, and never captures secret values. Absence is not a warning.

### Fixed

- `ashlr doctor`'s MCP probe no longer leaves bun processes running. It killed only the direct child, so when `bun` on PATH was a shell shim (pnpm or npm global installs) the real bun survived as a grandchild, and when the total probe cap fired first nothing was killed at all. Probes now run the bun binary that runs doctor, in their own process group, and the whole group is killed on timeout or when the cap fires. `runWithTimeout` takes an optional abort signal for this.
- Path refusals ("refused path outside working directory") now come back with `isError: true` from every tool, so hosts and agents see a failed call. Most tools returned the refusal as an ordinary successful result.
- `ashlr__write` accepts `path` as well as `filePath`, the name `ashlr__read` and `ashlr__edit` use. Called with `path`, it used to fail with `EISDIR` because the missing `filePath` resolved to the project folder. A missing path or non-string content now returns a clear error.
- The block message from the Write, NotebookEdit and other redirect hooks names the right setting: `ASHLR_HOOK_MODE=nudge`, or `"hookMode": "nudge"` in `~/.ashlr/config.json`. It used to suggest putting the environment variable name in that file.
- The router reports the plugin version in MCP `serverInfo` and its startup line instead of `dev`. `ASHLR_VERSION` still overrides it.

install.claude:
curl -fsSL https://plugin.ashlr.ai/install.sh | bash
/plugin marketplace add ashlrai/ashlr-plugin
/plugin install ashlr@ashlr-marketplace
/reload-plugins
install.codex:
git clone https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-plugin
cd ashlr-plugin && bun install
codex plugin marketplace add ashlrai/ashlr-plugin
codex plugin add ashlr@ashlr-marketplace
bun run scripts/cli.ts codex-doctor --json
install.cursor:
git clone https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-plugin
cd ashlr-plugin
bun install
ASHLR_ROOT="/home/you/ashlr-plugin"
sed "s|<ASHLR_PLUGIN_ROOT>|$ASHLR_ROOT|g" \
ports/cursor/mcp.json > ~/.cursor/mcp.json
install.goose:
git clone https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-plugin
cd ashlr-plugin
bun install
ASHLR_ROOT="/home/you/ashlr-plugin"
sed "s|<ASHLR_PLUGIN_ROOT>|$ASHLR_ROOT|g" \
ports/goose/recipe.yaml > my-ashlr-recipe.yaml

goose run --recipe my-ashlr-recipe.yaml

tools.name: ashlr__glob
tools.description: Token-efficient glob pattern matching. Returns compressed output instead of raw file lists: ≤20 matches listed verbatim; >20 matches grouped by top-level directory with counts and sample paths. Honors .gitignore automatically inside git repos (uses `git ls-files`), otherwise walks the filesystem while skipping node_modules, dist, build, .git, .next, .cache, .turbo, __pycache__, .venv. Replaces the native Glob tool ; produces 70-90% fewer tokens on large repos.

tools.name: ashlr__tree
tools.description: Token-efficient project structure view. One call returns a Unicode box-drawing tree with per-directory size/file-count and optional per-file LOC. Honors .gitignore automatically inside git repos, otherwise skips a standard exclusion set (node_modules, dist, build, .git, .next, .cache, .turbo, __pycache__, .venv). Replaces the 3-5 orientation calls (ls -la + find + multiple Reads) Claude Code normally makes when opening a repo.

tools.name: ashlr__ls
tools.description: Gitignore-aware directory listing. Compact columnar output with elision past maxEntries (default 80). Set bypassSummary:true to see all entries.

tools.name: ashlr__diff
tools.description: Fast adaptive git diff. Use instead of native Bash 'git diff | cat' when reviewing changes ; avoids dumping thousands of lines into context. Compresses by auto-selecting stat-only (>500 changed lines), stat+hottest-hunks (100–500), or full patch (<100); typical savings 60–95% on large diffs. Accepts any git ref plus pseudo-refs 'staged', 'unstaged', 'working'. For refactor/rename reviews use ashlr__diff_semantic instead.

tools.name: ashlr__webfetch
tools.description: Token-efficient URL fetcher. Aggressively extracts article text from HTML (title + main content, strips nav/scripts/styles), pretty-prints + array-elides JSON, byte-caps plain text. Default cap 100 KB vs native WebFetch which is uncapped. Use instead of WebFetch when you want article content ; saves 60-95% tokens on typical pages.

tools.name: ashlr__read
tools.description: Read a file with snipCompact truncation (head + tail, elided middle). Use instead of native Read when the file is >2KB ; avoids returning the full payload; compresses by preserving only the structurally significant head and tail; typical savings 60–90% on large files. Pass bypassSummary:true to get the full file when you need it.

tools.name: ashlr__flush
tools.description: Flush all queued ashlr__edit writes to disk immediately and return a summary of what was committed. Use when you need to read a file you just edited, or at the end of a multi-edit sequence.

tools.name: ashlr__edit_structural
tools.description: Rename a symbol with AST awareness (one file or N files). Use instead of native Edit when renaming variables/functions/types ; avoids accidental matches in strings/comments. Compresses by returning only a rename summary; typical savings 80–95%. operation='rename': file-local. operation='rename-cross-file': across rootDir. operation='extract-function': extract byte-range to new function. Supports .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx. dryRun=true previews. Use ashlr__edit for literal edits.

tools.name: ashlr__rename_file
tools.description: Rename (move) a source file AND update every import specifier in the project that resolved to it. Handles extension elision ('./foo' → './bar'), directory-index resolution ('./foo' when foo/index.ts), and skips bare package specifiers. Refuses if 'to' already exists, 'to's parent directory is missing, paths escape cwd, or either path is a binary file. Supports dryRun. Complements ashlr__edit_structural (which renames identifiers, not module paths).

tools.name: ashlr__search_replace_regex
tools.description: Regex-based bulk substitution across files in one call. Use instead of native Edit when patterns are mechanical (X→Y across many call sites) ; native Edit doesn't support regex. Compresses by returning a per-file match-count summary; typical savings 80–95%. Global flag is implicit; supports i/m/s/u; capture groups ($1, $2, $&) in replacement. Use dryRun=true to preview. For literal single-file edits use ashlr__edit. For AST-aware renames use ashlr__edit_structural.

tools.name: ashlr__websearch
tools.description: Token-efficient web search wrapper. Deduplicates results by domain, truncates snippets to ~500 chars, and synthesizes a 1-paragraph summary when more than 3 results are returned. Use instead of WebSearch to save 40-80% tokens on search result payloads. Args: query (required), maxResults (default 5), summarize (default true).

tools.name: ashlr__task_list
tools.description: Token-efficient task list viewer. Filters by status/owner, limits to max rows (default 30), and returns a compact column view: taskId, status, subject (80 chars), ageMin. Use instead of TaskList to avoid verbose task payloads. Args: status (optional filter), owner (optional filter), limit (default 30).

tools.name: ashlr__task_get
tools.description: Token-efficient single task viewer. Fetches a task by ID and snipCompacts the description if it exceeds 2KB (head + tail with elision marker). Returns: taskId, status, subject, descriptionCompact, fullLength. Use instead of TaskGet for long-description tasks. Args: taskId (required).

tools.name: ashlr__notebook_edit
tools.description: Edit a single cell in a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb). Use instead of native NotebookEdit when the notebook is >5KB or has many unrelated cells ; only the edited cell and its immediate neighbors are returned, with `[N cells unchanged]` for the rest. The full notebook is never echoed. Typical savings: 65-75% on multi-cell notebooks. Args: notebookPath, cellIndex, newSource, cellType (optional: code|markdown).

tools.name: ashlr__pipe
tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] Executes model-authored JS code server-side ; off by default, enable with ASHLR_PIPE_ENABLE=1. Run a JS expression that calls ctx.{grep,read,ls,glob} internally ; intermediate results NEVER enter context, only the return value does. Typical 80–95% token savings vs calling tools individually. ctx methods accept the same args as the ashlr__ tools they wrap. ctx.bash requires the additional ASHLR_PIPE_ALLOW_BASH=1 flag. Example: `return await ctx.grep({pattern:'TODO',cwd:'my project'});` returns the grep tool's text output as a string, which may include status messages.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_state
tools.description: Read fleet lane targets and holds, the last 20 job states and latest leader event from ~/.ashlr/fleet/{targets.json,holds.json,jobs.jsonl,leader-events.jsonl}. Read-only; missing or invalid files are reported as unavailable. Never opens environment or secret files.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_events
tools.description: Read typed events from ~/.ashlr/dispatch-events.log and ~/.ashlr/metrics/jobs.jsonl. JSON records or timestamped dispatch text; complete lines only, dispatch source first. Opaque per-source cursor supports polling; limit defaults to 200 (maximum 200). Missing, unsafe and malformed files are reported without raw contents. Read-only.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_intent
tools.description: Append an audited pending request to ~/.ashlr/fleet/intents.jsonl; never execute it. pause/resume require lane; kill requires job_id; reassign requires job_id and lane; set-slot requires lane and slots (0–1024). All requests require requested_by (caller-supplied attribution) and reason. No other fields or paths accepted.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_session
tools.description: Read a fleet job's latest metadata and metrics, PR URL, worktree and last 150 log lines from ~/.ashlr/fleet/jobs.jsonl and logs/<job_id>.log. Token-like strings are redacted; missing or unsafe files are reported. Read-only; accepts a job ID, never a path.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_act
tools.description: Request fleet pause/resume (lane), kill (job_id), reassign (job_id, lane), slots (lane, slots 0–1024), or steer (job_id, message). Requires requested_by (caller attribution) and reason. dry_run defaults true: audit preview only. false appends a pending controller request, never claims execution. All valid calls append to ~/.ashlr/fleet/actions.jsonl; controller execution is external. No caller-selected paths.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_snapshot
tools.description: Read the ~/.ashlr/fleet snapshot as structured JSON: lanes (targets and holds), complete job upserts beyond the 20-row UI tail, job-reported PR links, the latest leader event and per-source errors. Pass the opaque cursor from a previous response to get only net changes and removed ids. Missing or unsafe sources are null with error entries. Read-only; accepts an optional cursor, never paths.

tools.name: ashlr__fleet_direction
tools.description: Read the project direction (VISION.md by default, or another top-level *.md filename via direction) and append governed proposals to DIRECTION-PROPOSED.md in the project root. propose requires author and text (at most 8192 characters); proposals are suggestions, never adopted direction. MASON-INBOX.md and VISION.md stay protected: DIRECTION-PROPOSED.md is the only writable file, under nofollow and single-link checks. No caller-selected paths.

tools.name: ashlr__grep
tools.description: Search for a pattern. Use instead of native Grep always ; genome-aware when .ashlrcode/genome/ exists (returns only the most relevant pre-summarized sections + merged PRs + closed issues), falls back to ripgrep with LLM summarization for large result sets. Compresses by filtering to relevant chunks; typical savings 70–90%.

tools.name: ashlr__edit
tools.description: Single literal search/replace in one file, returns only a diff summary. Use instead of native Edit when the file is >5KB or the combined before/after is >=80 chars ; avoids the full file round-trip. Compresses by returning only the changed lines; typical savings 80%. In strict mode (default) requires exactly one match. For many edits across files use ashlr__multi_edit instead. For symbol renames use ashlr__edit_structural instead.

tools.name: ashlr__write
tools.description: Write content to a file without echoing the full content back. If the file already exists, delegates to ashlr__edit (full-file replace, compact diff response). If the file is new, creates it and returns a compact acknowledgment (path, bytes, sha8). Either way, the full file content is never returned ; ~80% token savings vs native Write.

tools.name: ashlr__http
tools.description: HTTP fetch with compressed output. Readable-extracts main content from HTML, pretty-prints + array-elides JSON, bounded byte cap. Refuses non-http/https schemes and private hosts by default.

tools.name: ashlr__logs
tools.description: Tail a log file efficiently. Reads the last N lines (default 200), detects severity from bracketed tags, bare prefixes, JSON/logfmt level fields, and Python tracebacks, filters by level and/or ISO timestamp, and collapses runs of identical consecutive lines into '(42x) ...'. Supports glob paths. Lines with no parseable timestamp are skipped (never fatal) when 'since' is set.

tools.name: ashlr__sql
tools.description: Run SQL against SQLite or Postgres and get a compact, token-dense text result. Replaces the typical 3-4 Bash calls (psql / sqlite3 + parse stdout) with one tool call. Supports SELECT, DDL, DML, EXPLAIN, and a schema-introspection mode.

tools.name: ashlr__diff_semantic
tools.description: AST-aware (heuristic) git diff summarization. A 200-line rename-refactor across 20 files renders as one line. Detects: symbol renames across >= 3 files, signature-only changes, formatting-only diffs. Degrades gracefully to compact diff output when no semantic patterns are found. Use instead of ashlr__diff when reviewing refactors, renames, or large reformatting commits.

tools.name: ashlr__pr
tools.description: Fetch a GitHub PR and return a compact review-ready summary (header, reviews, unresolved comments, status checks). Read-only ; never approves, comments, or merges. Saves 60-90% of the tokens a raw `gh pr view` dump would cost.

tools.name: ashlr__issue
tools.description: Fetch a GitHub issue and return a compact header + body + comment list. In 'thread' mode, each comment is rendered with snipCompact on > 500 char bodies. Read-only.

tools.name: ashlr__pr_comment
tools.description: Post a comment on a GitHub PR. Pass pr:"current" to target the PR for the checked-out branch. Returns the new comment URL.

tools.name: ashlr__pr_approve
tools.description: Approve a GitHub PR with an optional review body. Refuses to approve your own PR. Pass pr:"current" to target the PR for the checked-out branch.

tools.name: ashlr__issue_create
tools.description: Create a new GitHub issue with title + body and optional labels/assignees. Returns the new issue number and URL.

tools.name: ashlr__issue_close
tools.description: Close a GitHub issue with an optional closing comment and reason (completed|not_planned).

tools.name: ashlr__genome_propose
tools.description: Queue a proposed update to a named genome section. Fire-and-forget: the proposal is appended to the pending queue and will be merged into the genome on the next ashlr__genome_consolidate call. Use this to record project decisions, new strategies, architectural discoveries, or lessons learned so they persist across sessions.

tools.name: ashlr__genome_consolidate
tools.description: Merge pending proposals into the genome. Without `model` (and without $ASHLR_LLM_URL) runs a deterministic sequential-apply; with an LLM configured by $ASHLR_LLM_URL it merges conflicting proposals for the same section.

tools.name: ashlr__genome_status
tools.description: Show pending proposals and recent mutations for the current genome. Compact report suitable for inline context.

tools.name: ashlr__multi_edit
tools.description: Many edits across multiple files in one atomic call. Use instead of N separate Edit or ashlr__edit calls when touching more than one file ; N round-trips collapse to 1, with full rollback on any failure. Compresses by returning one consolidated diff summary; typical savings (N−1) × per-call overhead. For a single file use ashlr__edit instead. For symbol renames use ashlr__edit_structural instead.

tools.name: ashlr__orient
tools.description: Meta-orientation tool. Answers 'how does X work here?' in a single call: runs a project tree scan, derives keywords from your query, discovers relevant files (genome retriever if .ashlrcode/genome/ exists, else ripgrep), snipCompacts them, and asks a local LLM for a ≤600-char synthesis plus a suggested next tool call. Replaces 3-5 round-trips (tree + grep + multiple reads). Read-only.

tools.name: ashlr__bash
tools.description: Run a shell command. Use instead of native Bash when the command produces verbose output (git log, test runners, npm install, find, ps). Auto-compresses stdout > 2KB and emits compact structured summaries for common commands (git status, ls, find, npm ls). stderr is never compressed. Refuses catastrophic patterns; use ashlr__read for cat. Typical savings 60–90% on verbose commands.

tools.name: ashlr__bash_start
tools.description: Spawn a long-running shell command in the background and return a session id. Use ashlr__bash_tail to poll incremental output, ashlr__bash_stop to kill, ashlr__bash_list to enumerate. Ideal for watchers, tails, long builds, and anything where streaming >> one-shot.

tools.name: ashlr__bash_tail
tools.description: Read new stdout/stderr since the last poll for a background session. Auto-compresses the tail window when > 2KB. If wait_ms > 0, blocks (event-driven) until output arrives or the process exits, up to that ceiling.

tools.name: ashlr__bash_stop
tools.description: Kill a background session by id. Sends SIGTERM (configurable) and escalates to SIGKILL after 2s if still alive.

tools.name: ashlr__bash_list
tools.description: List active background sessions: id | pid | started | cumulative bytes | command.

tools.name: ashlr__test
tools.description: Run a test suite and return structured, token-efficient failure output. Supports bun test, vitest, jest, pytest, go test, and a generic fallback. Parses runner output into pass/fail/skip counts plus per-failure file:line + message + stack ; eliminating the read-source-fix-rerun loop that wastes 25–30% of tokens on test-driven workflows.

tools.name: ashlr__savings
tools.description: Show estimated tokens and cost saved by ashlr tools in the current session and lifetime totals. Use instead of manually counting tool calls to measure ashlr efficiency.

tools.name: ashlr__ask
tools.description: Single-tool entry point for ashlr. Accepts a natural-language question and auto-routes to the correct underlying tool (ashlr__read, ashlr__grep, ashlr__orient, ashlr__tree, or ashlr__glob) using deterministic rules ; no LLM in the routing step. Output always starts with a one-line trace showing which tool fired and why.

commands.name: ashlr-allow
commands.description: Auto-approve every ashlr MCP tool so Claude Code stops prompting in bypass-permissions mode.

commands.name: ashlr-benchmark
commands.description: Run the ashlr-plugin token-savings benchmark against the current project.

commands.name: ashlr-brief
commands.description: Toggle response-shortening (caveman-inspired, ashlr-flavored) with three intensity levels. Trims filler from Claude's prose to save 30–55% on output tokens while keeping code blocks, errors, and destructive-action confirmations in full grammar.

commands.name: ashlr-budget
commands.description: Set, check, or clear a session spend cap. Guards against runaway tool use in long sessions.

commands.name: ashlr-compact
commands.description: Identify stale tool results accumulating in the conversation history and surface a recompression plan.

commands.name: ashlr-dashboard
commands.description: Rich token-savings dashboard ; per-tool bar charts, 7d/30d sparklines, projected annual savings, and cost in dollars.

commands.name: ashlr-doctor
commands.description: Diagnose an ashlr-plugin install ; checks plugin path, version, MCP servers, hooks, stats, genome, and settings in under 10 seconds.

commands.name: ashlr-eco-mode
commands.description: Toggle eco mode ; aggressive token-saving behaviors that trade some response richness for lower session cost.

commands.name: ashlr-fleet
commands.description: Explain the Phantom fleet pane, local peers, and governed Claude model routing.

commands.name: ashlr-genome-init
commands.description: Initialize a `.ashlrcode/genome/` in the current project so ashlr__grep can route through genome RAG for ~-84% token savings.

commands.name: ashlr-genome-keygen
commands.description: Generate an X25519 keypair for team-cloud genome v2 encryption and register the public half with Ashlr. Run this once per machine before running /ashlr-genome-team-init. Safe to re-run ; a no-op when the machine's key is already registered.

commands.name: ashlr-genome-loop
commands.description: Inspect and control the automatic genome propose + consolidate loop (PostToolUse observer + SessionEnd consolidator).

commands.name: ashlr-genome-push
commands.description: Push the local .ashlrcode/genome/ to the team cloud. Safe to run any time; invoked automatically at SessionEnd after consolidation. No-op when the repo has no .cloud-id (i.e. team-genome not initialized) or when ASHLR_CLOUD_GENOME_DISABLE=1.

commands.name: ashlr-genome-rewrap
commands.description: Re-wrap the team-cloud genome DEK for every member with a current pubkey. Run this after a teammate rotates their keypair (/ashlr-genome-keygen --force) or joins the team and runs /ashlr-genome-keygen for the first time. Admin-only.

commands.name: ashlr-genome-team-init
commands.description: Initialize (or rewrap for new members of) a team-cloud genome for the current repo. One-time per repo by an admin; then teammates join via /ashlr-team-invite + /ashlr-genome-keygen + admin re-runs with --wrap-all.

commands.name: ashlr-handoff
commands.description: Generate a context-pack for the next session to resume cold.

commands.name: ashlr-help
commands.description: List every ashlr slash command with a one-line description, grouped by category.

commands.name: ashlr-hook-timings
commands.description: Show per-hook latency report (p50/p95/max) from hook-timings.jsonl.

commands.name: ashlr-leaderboard
commands.description: Opt in or out of the public ashlr savings leaderboard at plugin.ashlr.ai/community. Opt-in is OFF by default; when on, your GitHub handle and total tokens/$ saved are shown publicly (never your email). Requires a signed-in account that syncs stats (Pro/Team).

commands.name: ashlr-legend
commands.description: Decode every element of the ashlr status line (plain-text legend).

commands.name: ashlr-ollama-setup
commands.description: Diagnose and guide local Ollama install so `/ashlr-genome-init --summarize` works reliably. Recommends a fast 3B model and smoke-tests it.

commands.name: ashlr-orchestrate-status
commands.description: Inspect past /ashlr-orchestrate runs ; list recent runs or drill into a single graph by id.

commands.name: ashlr-orchestrate
commands.description: Distributed-orchestration MVP ; expand a goal into a task graph, preview the DAG, confirm, and run it (Pro / Team only).

commands.name: ashlr-parallelize
commands.description: Spawn N parallel sub-agents ; one per file ; each applying the same task instruction. Merges results into a unified report.

commands.name: ashlr-report-crash
commands.description: Upload a recent ashlr-plugin crash dump to the maintainer. Opt-in, already-redacted, one report per invocation. Gives the founder faster bug signal when something in the plugin threw.

commands.name: ashlr-resume
commands.description: Resume your last coding session ; shows what you were doing, which files were active, and suggested next steps.

commands.name: ashlr-savings
commands.description: Show estimated tokens and cost saved by the ashlr-plugin this session and lifetime.

commands.name: ashlr-selftest
commands.description: Run every ashlr command's entry point against a throwaway fixture repo with --json and report pass/fail per command.

commands.name: ashlr-settings
commands.description: View or change ashlr-plugin settings.

commands.name: ashlr-spawn
commands.description: Spawn a named delegation pattern as one or more sub-agents. Patterns defined in _spawn-patterns.json.

commands.name: ashlr-status
commands.description: Report the ashlr-plugin activation status and MCP server health.

commands.name: ashlr-team-invite
commands.description: Invite someone to your ashlr team by email. Sends a magic-link invite (admin role required).

commands.name: ashlr-tier
commands.description: Three-phase tiered delegation ; explore (haiku) → implement (sonnet) → integration-check (haiku). Routes each phase to the right model tier automatically.

commands.name: ashlr-tour
commands.description: 60-second guided walkthrough of the ashlr-plugin on the current project ; proves the value of the tools on real files.

commands.name: ashlr-update
commands.description: Update the ashlr-plugin to the latest version from its git remote.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-brief
workflowSkills.description: Tunable response-shortening skill for Claude Code. Trims filler from prose to reduce output tokens 30–55% while preserving grammar and code fidelity. Three intensity levels (lite / standard / concise). Auto-clarity exceptions for security, destructive actions, errors, and code blocks.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-codex-doctor
workflowSkills.description: Check Ashlr's Codex plugin packaging, MCP manifest, hooks, skills, and workspace allow-list. Use when Codex setup, plugin loading, or MCP registration looks wrong.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-codex-efficient-tools
workflowSkills.description: Codex-native efficient tool workflow. Prefer Ashlr MCP read, grep, tree, bash, savings, and genome tools before native scans when they reduce context.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-codex-genome-refresh
workflowSkills.description: Refresh or maintain Ashlr project genome state from Codex. Use after architectural changes, schema/routing changes, or substantial refactors.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-codex-parallel-explore
workflowSkills.description: Efficient parallel exploration habits for Codex. Use when a task needs several independent codebase questions answered before implementation.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-codex-savings
workflowSkills.description: Inspect Ashlr token savings from Codex using host-neutral CLI and MCP surfaces.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-cost-refactor
workflowSkills.description: Token-efficient refactoring discipline for Claude Code. Diff-first before editing, structural edits for renames, find-all-refs then one multi_edit per file, no re-reads between edits, one genome proposal at the end. Reduces refactor session cost 40–65%.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-efficient
workflowSkills.description: Output structure reshaper for Claude Code. Complements ashlr-brief's prose trimming by enforcing inverted-pyramid order, inline code for identifiers, tables for multi-item comparisons, and no transitional filler. Works standalone or alongside ashlr-brief.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-genome-author
workflowSkills.description: Guidelines for when and how to call ashlr__genome_propose to keep the project genome accurate. Covers post-architectural-decision proposals, correct summary format, and what NOT to propose. Keeps the genome signal-rich without noise.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-lean-tools
workflowSkills.description: Highest-impact token-saving habits for Claude Code tool use. Read-once, batch edits, orient-before-search, skip verification reads, grep-before-read, concise output at high spend. Reduces session token cost 30–60%.

workflowSkills.name: ashlr-search
workflowSkills.description: Genome-aware search habits for Claude Code. Prefer ashlr__grep and ashlr__glob over native scans; compose multi-term queries; trust genome summaries; orient once before searching. Reduces redundant reads and search token cost 40–70%.
